title: Fibre flatness detects finite freeness near a relatively flat point
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to Y$ be locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $M$ be a quasi-coherent module on the small etale ringed site of $X$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], of finite presentation: etale locally $M$ is the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n$ with $m,n$ finite. Use tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] and point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Fix $x\in|X|$ and suppose that $M$ is flat over $Y$ at $x$: on every compatible etale scheme-chart diagram $U\to V$ over $X\to Y$, the ordinary module stalk at each $u$ over $x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{V,v}$. Module flatness means exactness of tensoring [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For any field $K$ [def-weil-field] and representative $\xi:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ of $x$, put $y_K=f\xi$, $X_{y_K}=X\times_{Y,y_K}\operatorname{Spec}K$, and let $M_{y_K}$ be the pullback of $M$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The map $(\xi,\mathrm{id})$ defines a point $\widetilde x$ of $X_{y_K}$. Then the following are equivalent: (i) there are an etale scheme neighbourhood $e:U\to X$ whose point image contains $x$ and an integer $r\geq0$ such that $e^*M\simeq\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$; (ii) $M_{y_K}$ is flat over $X_{y_K}$ at $\widetilde x$, in the same chartwise module sense with the identity of $X_{y_K}$ as structure map. The equivalence holds for every choice of $K$ and $\xi$, including $M=0$ and $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0CZS (lemma-flat-and-free-at-point-fibre), equivalence (1) and (4); Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), equivalence (1) and (2), applied to id_X over Y, replaces the geometric representative by any field-valued representative.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $V_0\to Y$, then a surjective etale scheme chart $U_0\to X\times_YV_0$. The atlas, fibre-product, and etale-permanence statements give a compatible scheme map $U_0\to V_0$ and a point $u$ above $x$. Choose an affine open $V\subseteq V_0$ containing the image of $u$, and an affine open $U\subseteq U_0$ containing $u$ and mapping into $V$. Their composites $a:U\to X$ and $b:V\to Y$ are etale: open immersions are etale and etale maps compose. The chart definition of local finite presentation makes $U\to V$ locally of finite presentation. On these affine opens its section-ring map is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. Moreover $U\to V$ is a morphism of affine schemes, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. It is therefore of finite presentation, not merely locally so. Put $v$ for the image of $u$.

source.place: Tag 0CZS (lemma-flat-and-free-at-point-fibre), proof of (1) implies (4) by etale charts and the scheme case, and (4) implies (1); Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), (2) equivalent to (3).

proof.text: Since $a$ is etale, the tensor pullback $a^*M$ is the restriction of $M$ to the localized etale site [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]; it is quasi-coherent [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. Let $G$ be the Zariski quasi-coherent module corresponding to $a^*M$ by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. This restriction preserves the etale local finite presentation of $M$; [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] then gives finite presentation of $G$ in the Zariski sense. By the relative-flatness hypothesis, $G_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{V,v}$. Assume (ii). Apply [lem-sfb-space-fibre-flatness-chart-comparison] to $X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ and the diagram $U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}U\to V$. It says exactly that $(G_v)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{U_v,u}$. The pullback comparison in the Zariski-etale equivalence identifies this $G_v$ with the ordinary scheme-fibre pullback. The finite-presentation morphism $U\to V$ from step 1, the finite-presentation module $G$, and these two flatness assertions satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-trf-flat-fibre-free-neighbourhood]. Obtain an open $W\subseteq U$ containing $u$ and $r\geq0$ with $G|_W\cong\mathcal O_W^{\oplus r}$. The equivalence identifies the associated free module with $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus r}$: its formula on every etale test is tensor pullback of this finite direct sum. Thus $(a|_W)^*M\cong\mathcal O_W^{\oplus r}$. Since $W\to U$ is an open immersion, its composite with $a$ is etale and its point image contains $x$. This proves (i).

source.place: Tag 0CZS (lemma-flat-and-free-at-point-fibre), proof of (1) implies (4) by etale charts and the scheme case, and (4) implies (1); Tag 05WY (lemma-flat-on-fibres-at-point), (2) equivalent to (3).

proof.text: Conversely suppose (i), witnessed by $e:E\to X$ and $e^*M\cong\mathcal O_E^{\oplus r}$. Repeat the chart construction of step 1 with $E$ in place of $X$: choose $V\to Y$ surjective etale and a scheme chart of $E\times_YV$, with a point $u$ over a chosen point of $E$ above $x$. The resulting compatible etale chart $a:U\to X$ factors through $E$. Its pullback module is finite free: writing $a=e\circ p$, the tensor pullback along etale maps is restriction [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], so $a^*M\cong p^*e^*M\cong p^*\mathcal O_E^{\oplus r}$, and in tensor coordinates, $B\otimes_A A^r\cong B^r$, with $b\otimes(a_i)\mapsto(ba_i)$ and inverse $(b_i)\mapsto\sum_i b_i\otimes e_i$. The same formula for the scheme fibre over $v\in V$ makes $(G_v)_u\cong\mathcal O_{U_v,u}^r$, using the pullback comparison of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. A finite free module is flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fibre-flatness-chart-comparison] to $\mathrm{id}_X$ over $Y$ and $U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}U\to V$ to deduce (ii) for the prescribed $K,\xi$. Since that comparison holds for every representative, the equivalence has the asserted choice independence. Every construction allows $r=0$ and the zero module; no nonvanishing hypothesis was used.
